item.text: I’ll inspect the service documentation first, then enumerate all order pages with retry/rate-limit handling, cache customer records, compute the UTC-filtered reconciliation exactly, and validate both output files.

item.aggregated_output:
Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

item.text: The docs confirm 50-item pagination, bearer authentication, and customer-level percentage discounts. I’m implementing retries for both token expiry and rate limiting, while tracking every repeated order listing separately from the distinct qualifying-order count.

The reconciliation completed across all advertised pages, including 20 repeated listings. The computed result is 407 distinct qualifying orders totaling 9,329,707 cents; I’m doing the final schema and arithmetic checks now, then I’ll remove the working script and create the required Copper Heron marker.
